title: microchunk kernel coalescer and prefill backpressure estimator to reduce kernel churn and tail latency
author: Sofia Martinez
commits: 4a7f3d2 - introduce MicroChunkCoalescer and initial kernel coalescing hook
c2d8f5b - integrate estimator with continuous batching scheduler and KV primer
b5e2a44 - optimize CUDA kernel launch path to accept coalesced micro-chunks
f1a9c66 - perf tests, docs, and rollout/rollback scripts
description:
Background: We observed increased kernel-launch churn for short prefill bursts on models with mixed short/long context requests. Kernel launch overhead and tiny decode kernels led to 95th/99th tail latency spikes during bursty workloads. This PR introduces two complementary runtime changes: (1) a MicroChunk kernel coalescer that aggregates adjacent micro-prefill work items into larger kernel-friendly chunks before dispatch, and (2) a Prefill Backpressure Estimator that observes request arrival patterns and current KV priming state to delay noncritical prefill micro-chunks until they can be coalesced or merged with imminent decode work.

What this changes: single continuous string with sections. The implementation touches the scheduler, the batching layer, KV priming logic, and kernel invocation path: - MicroChunkCoalescer: lightweight, lock-free queue-level coalescing implemented in runtime/scheduler. It merges micro-prefill items when their cumulative token count and memory footprint fit an empirically tuned kernel-friendly window. Coalescing is conservative: it never exceeds configured per-GPU microchunk_target_tokens and is disabled for requests marked low-latency. - PrefillBackpressureEstimator: records prefix arrival inter-arrival times, KV cache warmness, and in-flight decode deadlines. It uses an EWMA+quantile heuristic to estimate whether waiting up to prefill_coalesce_delay_ms can increase coalescing opportunities without violating SLOs. - Kernel adaptor changes: coalescer emits contiguous memory-backed work descriptors so the CUDA adaptor can issue single combined kernels, reducing kernel launches. - Scheduler integration: continuous-batching scheduler now consults estimator and coalescer to decide early-merge vs immediate dispatch.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for estimator heuristics (runtime/kv) - [x] Integration tests for coalescing + kernel path (tests/perf) - [x] Benchmarks against bursty trace (benchmarks/perf) - [x] Docs for ops flags and rollout plan (docs/ops) - [x] Feature flag guarded behind runtime.flags.microchunk_coalescer

Benchmarks (internal microbenchmark harness): - Workload: mixed 8/128/512 token prefill mix, 30% concurrent decodes - Baseline (main): 95th prefill latency 84ms, 99th 189ms, kernel launches per-second 4.7k - This PR: 95th prefill latency 69ms (-17.9%), 99th 156ms (-17.5%), kernel launches per-second 3.6k (-23.4%), steady-state throughput +8% on the mixed trace. Tail regressions for short-request-only traces were within noise.

Files changed (high level snippets): - runtime/scheduler/microchunk_coalescer.rs: add MicroChunkCoalescer with lock-free chunk builder and backpressure hook - runtime/kv/prefill_backpressure_estimator.rs: estimator that publishes a per-queue delay suggestion via shared metrics - runtime/kernels/coalescer_cuda.cu: combined kernel entrypoint and small path for single-chunk fallback - runtime/batching/continuous_batching.rs: consult estimator and coalescer before flush

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: increased latency for some ultra-low-latency requests when coalescing holds a micro-chunk. Mitigation: requests can opt-out via request header runtime.prefill_priority=low_latency and the estimator respects per-request deadlines. - Risk: a bug in memory layout causing an OOM in the combined kernel path. Mitigation: added strict guards in the coalescer and a fallback to the original per-microchunk kernels; added integration tests that run under small-device profiles.

Operational notes: The feature is behind runtime.flags.microchunk_coalescer and default-off for Dedicated in the initial rollout. Rollout plan: 1) Canary on internal perf-canary region (2% traffic) for 48h, 2) expand to 20% if no regressions, 3) enable by default for hosted API for models where bench gives win. Rollback plan: flip runtime.flags.microchunk_coalescer=false and revert scheduler hook.
comments: Arjun Patel (review): Can you add a microbenchmark that isolates coalescer behaviour for 1-2 token prefill bursts? Also please document the heuristics used by the estimator and a source of truth for the EWMA window sizes.
Sofia Martinez (author): Added microbenchmark and expanded estimator docs in docs/ops/prefill_backpressure.md; EWMA window defaults to 256 samples and is runtime-configurable.
Lena Kirov (review): Verified kernel launch reduction on perf-canary; asked for an additional integration test that toggles opt-out header.
Sofia Martinez (author): Added opt-out integration test and a CI job that runs it under small-device profiles.
Damien Zhou (approval): Looks good, landing after CI green and a short soak in canary.
release_notes: Introduce MicroChunkCoalescer and Prefill Backpressure Estimator to reduce kernel-launch overhead and tail latency for bursty prefill workloads. Feature gated behind runtime.flags.microchunk_coalescer. Expect ~15-25% fewer kernel launches and up to ~18% tail latency reduction on mixed traces.
